steps: Carbohydrates are organic compounds made up of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. In many carbohydrates, hydrogen and oxygen are present in the same ratio as in water (2:1).
Carbohydrates are classified into monosaccharides, disaccharides and polysaccharides according to the number of sugar units they contain.
Monosaccharides are the simplest carbohydrates and cannot be broken down into smaller sugar units by hydrolysis. They usually have a ring-shaped structure in solution.
Examples include glucose, fructose and galactose. Glucose is an important source of energy for cells and is produced during photosynthesis.
Disaccharides consist of two monosaccharide units joined together. They can be broken down by hydrolysis into their constituent simple sugars.

Sucrose consists of glucose and fructose; maltose consists of two glucose units; lactose consists of glucose and galactose. Sucrose is an important form in which sugar is transported in plants, while lactose is the sugar present in milk.

Polysaccharides are large molecules made of many monosaccharide units joined in long chains. Their chains may be straight or branched, and they are generally not sweet and do not dissolve readily in water.
Starch is a polysaccharide that stores food in plants. Glycogen stores glucose in animals, especially in the liver and muscles. Cellulose forms the cell walls of plants and provides support.
items.finalAnswer: Carbohydrates include simple monosaccharides, two-unit disaccharides and many-unit polysaccharides, which function in energy supply, transport, food storage and plant support.

steps: Fatty acids are organic acids that form the basic components of fats and oils. Each has a long hydrocarbon chain and a carboxyl (–COOH) group.
Fatty acids are of two types: saturated and unsaturated.

Saturated fatty acids have no double bonds between the carbon atoms in their hydrocarbon chains; the carbon atoms are joined by single bonds only. Fats rich in saturated fatty acids are generally solid at room temperature.
Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more double bonds between carbon atoms in their chains. Oils rich in unsaturated fatty acids are generally liquid at room temperature.
items.finalAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have only single carbon-to-carbon bonds, whereas unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon-to-carbon double bonds.
